messages:
maria: Ran a quick entropy scan across feature maps for new-model-v3 on the standard eval shard. Seeing huge entropy spread in mid/late layers, wondering if this explains the weird perf delta on GPTQ/AWQ runs. Attached numbers below.

maria: key snippet from the scan output:
```
layer  | mean_entropy | std_entropy | top_channels(>2*std)
11     | 4.2          | 0.5         | 3
17     | 3.9          | 0.6         | 6  <-- spike zones
18     | 6.8          | 1.7         | 22 <-- suspicious
27     | 5.5          | 1.3         | 15
28     | 7.1          | 1.9         | 26 <-- worst
```

maria: Quick bakeoff perf delta (eval ppl delta vs fp16 baseline):
- GPTQ4: overall +2.8% ppl, layers 18/28 contribute ~+1.8% each
- AWQ4: overall +1.6% ppl, but still spikes at same layers
- INT8 naive: overall +4.7% ppl, catastrophic on layer 28

raj: ugh. so these layers have concentrated high-entropy channels that quantizers collapse? :eyes:

olivia: yep. high entropy -> wide dynamic range -> quant scale/zero-point issues. two quick mitigations: per-channel clamp for the top-k channels OR skip quantizing those whole layers and keep fp16.

maria: tried a small patch: per-channel adaptive clamp with per-channel percentile (99.5th) instead of global max for layers 18 & 28. results on canary eval: ppl delta -> GPTQ4 down to +0.9%, AWQ4 down to +0.5%.

maria: config I used:
```
quant_overrides:
  - layer: 18
    mode: per_channel_clamp
    clamp_pct: 99.5
  - layer: 28
    mode: per_channel_clamp
    clamp_pct: 99.0
fallback_layers: []
```

dmitri: can you paste the per-channel hist for layer 28? curious if it's a few heads or evenly spread.

maria: pasted compressed summary: top 3 channels hold 65% of range mass; tails are long. Looks heady.

olivia: then another approach: head/block granularity quant (blocksize=64) + outlier-channel scaling. less perf hit than full-layer fp16.

kevin: what's the latency/cost impact of doing per-channel clamps on 2 layers? numbers pls.

maria: perf numbers (prod-like nodes):
- baseline GPTQ4 (no overrides): 1.00x latency, cost index 1.00
- GPTQ4 + per-channel clamp layers 18/28: 1.03x latency, cost ~1.02
- GPTQ4 + skip layers -> keep fp16 for 18/28: 1.12x latency, cost ~1.08
So clamp seems cheap, skip is heavy.

raj: sounds like clamp is the sweet spot. Any regression tests failing?

ci-bot: canary run 1745643250 completed: eval-ppl delta GPTQ4+clamp = +0.6%, AWQ4+clamp = +0.4%, QA regression none, smoke passed.

maria: CI looks good. propose rollout plan:
1) Canary (5% traffic) GPTQ4 + per-channel clamp for layers 18/28, monitor ppl and token-level regression hooks
2) 25% after 2 hours if no regressions
3) full after 24h with auto-rollback on ppl delta > 1.5%

olivia: add a lightweight monitoring eval that seeds examples targeting those channels (few synthetic prompts) so we catch subtle semantic drift.

maria: good call. I'll add an eval set of ~200 targeted prompts and wire the regression alerts.

dmitri: also drop a fallback plan to run AWQ4 for those layers only if clamp fails. AWQ seems slightly more robust per earlier runs.

kevin: thumbs up from infra side for the canary. note: ops wants the 99.5 clamp value logged and audited.

maria: will add audit logs + explicit config commit. thanks all. :thumbsup:

raj: nice investigation. can we generalize a small script to auto-propose clamp percentiles when entropy > threshold? avoids manual tuning.

maria: yep that's next. filing proto ticket now and will push a tiny autotune script to the quant toolchain.

ci-bot: ticket created: QNT-3221 - entropy-driven clamp autotuner

kevin: leaving a reminder to test this flow on dedicated pools (reserved capacity) — perf variance there can change thresholds.

maria: noted. will schedule dedicated-run tomorrow. closing thread for now unless new regressions pop up.
